title: STEM Student Engagement with University Resources Builds Social Capital and Sense of Belonging: An Asset-Based Focus Group Study
text_snippet: STEM Student Engagement with University Resources Builds Social Capital and Sense of Belonging: An Asset-Based Focus Group Study Background. Attrition from STEM programs remains a persistent challenge for universities globally. To better support student success and socio-academic integration, universities have developed a range of curricular and co-curricular resources. Much emphasis has been placed on the benefits of these resources; however, less is known about how students recognize, access, and realize these benefits. Guided by a capital-mediated agency model, this asset-based focus group study examined how university-provided resources support undergraduate STEM students’ use of capital. We conducted four parallel focus groups with 21 students at a Norwegian university and analyzed narratives using thematic analysis. Results. Students described using both curricular and co-curricular resources to build personal/emotional, social, and human resource capital that helped them navigate academic and personal challenges. Curricular resources, including mandatory assignments, fieldwork, and laboratory activities, supported disciplinary training and opportunities to develop relationships with peers. title: The Impact of the Erasmus+ Programme on Participation in Democratic Life, Common Values and Civic Engagement: A Study on Portuguese and Slovenian Adult Education Organisations
text_snippet: The Impact of the Erasmus+ Programme on Participation in Democratic Life, Common Values and Civic Engagement: A Study on Portuguese and Slovenian Adult Education Organisations Active citizenship is one of the four main goals of adult education (AE) policy in the European Union (EU). While previous research has shown that EU AE policy has increasingly prioritised economic objectives, studies also suggest that Erasmus+ supports broader social goals. This study investigates how Erasmus+ in AE contributes to promoting active citizenship in Portugal and Slovenia. A mixed-methods design was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative data. Quantitative data were collected through a survey of 179 AE organisations, while qualitative data were obtained through document analysis, focus groups, and individual interviews with 17 representatives of AE organisations and 9 adult learners. The findings highlight the important role of Erasmus+ in supporting the social goals of European AE policy and suggest positive contributions to social inclusion, civic competences, critical thinking, and participation opportunities for adult learners, particularly among vulnerable groups. title: Developmental–Confirmatory Psychometric Evaluation of a Digital Peer-Assessment Microteaching Rubric Using Many-Facet Rasch Measurement
text_snippet: Developmental–Confirmatory Psychometric Evaluation of a Digital Peer-Assessment Microteaching Rubric Using Many-Facet Rasch Measurement Digital peer-assessment systems can scale performance-based evaluation, but psychometric quality depends on how rubric criteria and rating categories function under rater-mediated use. This study used Many-Facet Rasch Measurement (MFRM) to evaluate and refine a microteaching rubric implemented in the Mobile Audience Response System (MOARS) and assess it in a subsequent cohort. In Cohort 1 (2024–2025; 27 preservice teachers, 331 peer rater–performance records), the baseline six-criterion, four-level rubric was examined through four MFRM specifications. The lowest category was used only five times, while the holistic overall-impression criterion showed comparatively low mean-square fit values and conceptual overlap with the analytic criteria. In this context, collapsing the two lowest categories and excluding the holistic criterion yielded a five-criterion, three-category analytical specification with ordered thresholds and performance separation of 2.98 (reliability = 0.90). In Cohort 2 (2025–2026; 18 preservice teachers, 209 peer rater–performance records), the refined rubric, with an integrated Developing level, was administered unchanged. title: Longitudinal Associations Between Homework and Examination Performance in Engineering Mathematics
text_snippet: Longitudinal Associations Between Homework and Examination Performance in Engineering Mathematics Generative artificial intelligence has renewed questions about whether take-home homework remains associated with performance on supervised assessments. This retrospective longitudinal study analyzed 759 student records from 15 cohorts of an engineering mathematics course (2009–2025). Annual Pearson correlations between homework and quiz, midterm-examination, and final-examination scores were calculated with 95% confidence intervals and pooled within three periods using inverse-variance-weighted Fisher transformations. Course-grade outcomes were treated separately because they could incorporate homework. Homework was positively associated with all three supervised outcomes in every cohort, although effect sizes varied across years. Pooled homework–final-examination correlations were 0.75 before COVID-19, 0.68 during 2020–2022, and 0.78 during 2023–2025. The difference between the latter periods was nonsignificant, Z = 1.70, p = 0.089, and remained nonsignificant under random-effects pooling (p = 0.303) and after excluding 25 all-zero records (p = 0.075). title: Preservice Early Childhood Teachers’ AI Literacy and Self-Efficacy in a Structured “Vibe Coding” Design Task: An Exploratory Pre–Post Study
text_snippet: Preservice Early Childhood Teachers’ AI Literacy and Self-Efficacy in a Structured “Vibe Coding” Design Task: An Exploratory Pre–Post Study This exploratory study examined a structured Vibe Coding task in preservice early childhood teacher education and its association with self-reported AI literacy, self-efficacy, attitudes toward AI, and technology acceptance. Vibe Coding was used in a qualified sense: participants created educational applications through natural-language prompting, then reviewed and revised the outputs. The task was implemented in two undergraduate courses using a convergent mixed-methods, single-group pre–post design without a comparison group. Quantitative analysis included 32 matched cases, while qualitative analysis drew on 26 reflective logbooks. All 32 participants also completed a researcher-designed, non-validated self-assessment rubric, reported descriptively. Paired-samples t-tests showed significant pre–post increases across all six self-report scales after Holm–Bonferroni correction. Effect sizes were large for AI literacy, self-efficacy, attitudes, and perceived ease of use, and moderate for perceived usefulness and behavioural intention. title: Student Motivation in Remote Laboratories: A Multi-Institution Self-Determination Theory Study in Food Science Education
text_snippet: Student Motivation in Remote Laboratories: A Multi-Institution Self-Determination Theory Study in Food Science Education Remote laboratories (RL) have expanded access to food science laboratory education while shifting students into more autonomous learning environments. Self-Determination Theory (SDT) suggests that motivation in such settings depends on whether psychological needs, particularly competence, are satisfied as students navigate hands-on learning with reduced instructor presence. This cross-sectional, multi-institution study examined motivational profiles of food science students (n = 110) who completed take-home RL kits at six U.S. universities, using the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory. In a linear mixed model accounting for institutional clustering (n = 109), perceived competence, utility value, and effort investment were each uniquely and positively associated with interest; in the corresponding single-level model, the three constructs jointly accounted for 57% of the variance in interest. A comparison by prior food engineering coursework (n = 94) yielded a significant multivariate effect that no single construct accounted for. title: Reflective Practice in Arts-Based Learning: Teaching Adults with Intellectual Disabilities in Inclusive Higher Education
text_snippet: Reflective Practice in Arts-Based Learning: Teaching Adults with Intellectual Disabilities in Inclusive Higher Education This paper explores the development and delivery of an inclusive higher education programme for adults with intellectual disabilities within an Irish university. The programme was developed between two academic departments within an Irish University, to provide this student cohort with access to university life, enabling them to study and graduate alongside their peers. Central to the study is a module in arts-based communication, which aims to support students’ expressive, emotional, and social engagement in learning. Adopting a reflective, practice-based approach, the paper draws on the experiences of an educator involved in teaching on the programme. Through critical reflection on teaching practice, the study examines how arts-based pedagogies can enhance communication, participation, and inclusive learning environments for students with intellectual disabilities. The findings highlight the transformative potential of arts-based learning in supporting not only skill development but also confidence, self-expression, and relational engagement. title: Who Gets to Belong? Inclusive School Leadership and the Professional Experience of Early Career Teachers
text_snippet: Who Gets to Belong? Inclusive School Leadership and the Professional Experience of Early Career Teachers This study found that inclusive school leadership shaped early career teachers’ (ECTs’) professional belonging, but its influence depended on whether leaders’ relational intent was supported by the organisational conditions in which it was enacted. Inclusive leadership was understood as the relational and structural practices through which leaders foster voice, psychological safety, and equitable access to support. This study adopted an instrumental case study design, situated in an Australian primary school. Semi-structured interviews with five ECTs were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, from which four themes were identified. Relational signalling from the principal shaped whether ECTs felt safe to voice uncertainty. Leadership functioned as emotional co-regulation in demanding moments, though its sustainability varied. Organisational routines produced a hidden curriculum through which ECTs learned when belonging was conditional. In high-stakes situations, guided participation actively drew ECTs into professional community practices. title: Block-Based Programming for Educational Robotics in Lower Secondary Education: An Exploratory Challenge-Based Learning Study
text_snippet: Block-Based Programming for Educational Robotics in Lower Secondary Education: An Exploratory Challenge-Based Learning Study Time-limited robotics assessments can misrepresent classroom performance when unfinished attempts are discarded or recorded as exact completion times. This exploratory study addresses a practical reporting need: describing immediate execution and post-task perceptions while retaining non-completion, rather than ranking educational technologies. Thirty-five novice lower-secondary students participated in an approximately 80 min challenge-based implementation in three intact cohorts (n=16, 11, and 8). A structured observation record and stopwatch captured completion of a movement-and-sensor task within 10 min; a six-item questionnaire captured task-specific perceptions. Completion proportions were 16/16, 11/11, and 5/8. Kaplan–Meier estimates and restricted mean time through 10 min yielded 3.05, 4.37, and 7.85 min, respectively. title: Rethinking Technology-Driven Sustainability Education Through Intermediality: Cultural Mediation, Literary and Artistic Humanities, and the Sustainable Development Goals
text_snippet: Rethinking Technology-Driven Sustainability Education Through Intermediality: Cultural Mediation, Literary and Artistic Humanities, and the Sustainable Development Goals The implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) across educational contexts has generated substantial research on pedagogies aligned with technology-driven sustainability education. Recent scholarship increasingly recognises that sustainability transitions require not only technological innovation but also cultural transformations capable of reshaping social norms, environmental imaginaries, and collective values. However, the processes through which sustainability meanings are mediated across different cultural and media environments remain insufficiently explored. This article argues that intermediality provides a valuable analytical framework for understanding how sustainability knowledge is produced, transformed, and experienced through interactions among literary, visual, performative, audiovisual, and digital media. To examine the visibility of such approaches within sustainability education research, the study employs a bibliometric and thematic mapping of the Web of Science Core Collection, focusing on humanities and cognate social science perspectives. title: Ubuntu Translanguaging as a Decolonizing Pedagogical Framework: Reimagining Multilingual Literacy Education for SDG 4
text_snippet: Ubuntu Translanguaging as a Decolonizing Pedagogical Framework: Reimagining Multilingual Literacy Education for SDG 4 This article advances Ubuntu translanguaging as a decolonizing pedagogical framework for multilingual literacy education, aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). Drawing on Ubuntu philosophy and translanguaging theory, it conceptualizes Ubuntu translanguaging as a relational, asset-based framework that challenges linguistic hierarchies and affirms learners’ full linguistic resources. Grounded in Ghanaian educational contexts, the framework responds to deficit narratives that overlook the community-rooted pedagogies multilingual teachers already use, and shows how multilingual pedagogies strengthen comprehension, affirm identity, and expand equitable participation in education. Three questions guide the article: how Ubuntu translanguaging challenges colonial language hierarchies in curricula and policy, how it operationalizes SDG 4’s commitments to inclusion and equity, and how it can inform Global South–North research partnerships built on mutual growth. By centering indigenous epistemologies and positioning teachers as co-researchers and co-creators of knowledge, the framework offers a reciprocal model for achieving SDG 4.

title: Project-Based Learning in Girls’ Physical Education: An Exploratory Two-Cohort Pilot Study of Physical Activity and Motor Performance
text_snippet: Project-Based Learning in Girls’ Physical Education: An Exploratory Two-Cohort Pilot Study of Physical Activity and Motor Performance Project-based learning (PBL) combines student-centred learning with motor practice, but evidence on physical activity and motor performance in school physical education remains limited. This exploratory pilot study compared PBL with teacher-led instruction in two non-randomised cohorts comprising 53 girls: 27 fifth-grade pupils in basketball and 26 seventh-grade pupils in aerobics. Each cohort included one intact class per condition. Outcomes included pre–post basketball motor tests, final aerobics performance and physical activity records from subsets of pupils. Motor comparisons were exploratory, and wearable outcomes were summarised descriptively at the class and lesson levels. The baseline-adjusted obstacle dribble test comparison favoured the control class (experimental-minus-control difference: +4.01 s; 95% CI: 1.88 to 6.14; Holm-adjusted p = 0.002); the other two basketball comparisons remained inconclusive. The final aerobics score difference was −0.49 points on a 0–16 scale (95% CI: −3.75 to 2.78). title: Exploring Authentic Partnership in Distance Initial Teacher Education: Associate Teachers’ Perspectives from Aotearoa New Zealand
text_snippet: Exploring Authentic Partnership in Distance Initial Teacher Education: Associate Teachers’ Perspectives from Aotearoa New Zealand Partnership is widely treated as central to high-quality practicum in Initial Teacher Education, yet most research assumes local, ongoing relationships between Initial Teacher Education providers and schools. This study explores how Associate Teachers understand authentic partnership with a distance Initial Teacher Education provider in Aotearoa New Zealand, where placements are geographically dispersed, and partnerships are often short-term. Guided by an interpretivist qualitative design, the study drew on an online survey (n = 30), online focus groups (n = 7), and a live poll used as an elicitation tool (n = 7). Analysis identified four interrelated themes: communication as the foundation of partnership, clarity of roles and responsibilities, bridging theory and practice, and partnership and perceived support for Māori. The findings show that partnership in distance Initial Teacher Education is not best understood as either wholly relational or purely procedural. Instead, it shifts along a relational–transactional continuum, with communication systems, role clarity, and shared pedagogical understanding shaping whether partnership is experienced as collaborative or fragmented. title: When a Six Does Not Appear: Prospective Primary Teachers’ Questions for Informal Statistical Inference
text_snippet: When a Six Does Not Appear: Prospective Primary Teachers’ Questions for Informal Statistical Inference Teachers’ questions shape how students use data, representations, and uncertainty, yet little is known about the inferential opportunities embedded in questions formulated by prospective primary teachers using a provided representation. This study analyzed 133 questions produced by 45 prospective primary teachers for sixth-grade students in a semi-structured problem-posing task based on a dotplot of 60 die rolls in which no six appeared and two contrasting interpretations. Using theory-informed content analysis, we found that, under the scaffolded task conditions, most questions combined generalization beyond the observed data, data as evidence, and probabilistic language. Explicit comparison of the two interpretations was uncommon in the wording of individual questions, while future or unobserved outcomes and the data-generating process were more frequent foci. Retrospective assessments and analytical classifications provided related but not fully equivalent perspectives on the formulated questions. title: Improving Students’ Digital Literacy in School Education: Insights and Practices from Physical Education Teachers
text_snippet: Improving Students’ Digital Literacy in School Education: Insights and Practices from Physical Education Teachers The integration of digital technologies into all areas of life, including school education, is a global megatrend. However, researchers note a lack of research on students’ digital literacy within school curricula, and specifically, it has not been examined in the context of school physical education. To address this research gap, this study explores physical education teachers’ practices, experiences, and perceived challenges in improving students’ digital literacy. This qualitative study is based on 29 semi-structured interviews with Latvian school physical education teachers, and an analytical framework for students’ digital literacy consisting of eight core domains was used to analyse the data. The results reveal a broad range of teaching practices reflecting constructivist and natural or ‘no formal teaching’ approaches. In assessing students’ digital literacy, formative and summative approaches were identified. Addressing gaps and challenges in improving students’ digital literacy, the following domains of teacher support needs were identified: conceptual, practical, and technical. title: Literacies of Transnational Students of Color: A Critical Interpretive Synthesis Through an Intersectionally Informed Critical Race Theory Lens
text_snippet: Literacies of Transnational Students of Color: A Critical Interpretive Synthesis Through an Intersectionally Informed Critical Race Theory Lens Although racialization profoundly shapes global education, literacy scholarship concerning transnational students of Color (TSCs) frequently lacks an intersectional lens. This critical interpretive synthesis examines how existing studies conceptualize TSCs’ literacies and how their characterizations of race structurally and ideologically de/legitimize these practices. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematically identified, screened, and selected empirical studies, then conducted a critical interpretive synthesis using an intersectionally informed Critical Race Theory framework, reported in accordance with ENTREQ. The review protocol was retrospectively documented and registered on the Open Science Framework. From 1282 initially identified records, 121 studies met the inclusion criteria. Our synthesis indicates that most studies frame literacy as an ideological, translocal, and translinguistic social practice. While outcome-driven institutional norms persistently perpetuate Eurocentric epistemologies, scholarship explicitly naming race exposes enduring colonial legacies. title: Navigating Inclusive Practices in Supporting Neurodivergent Learners in South African Under-Resourced Mainstream Schools: Perspectives from School Principals
text_snippet: Navigating Inclusive Practices in Supporting Neurodivergent Learners in South African Under-Resourced Mainstream Schools: Perspectives from School Principals Principals in mainstream schools occupy a pivotal yet underexplored position in supporting neurodivergent learners within resource-constrained settings. Guided by the transformational leadership theory lens, this study examines how mainstream school principals navigate neurodiversity support in resource-constrained school settings. A qualitative descriptive design, rooted in the interpretivist paradigm, was adopted. Data were collected from eighteen mainstream school principals from the Johannesburg Central district, using a quasi-structured questionnaire. Four themes emerged: identification of neurodivergent learners; support structures and inclusive practices; human, material resource and systemic constraints; and principals’ policy recommendations and visions for inclusive education in mainstream schools. The findings reveal a significant gap between policy intent and school-level practice. While a minority of principals demonstrated transformational leadership practices that produced meaningful inclusive outcomes, the majority are constrained by deep structural and systemic barriers that limit their capacity. title: Cultivating a Regional Geoscience Learning Ecosystem: Systemic Equity and Cultural Change in California’s Central Valley
text_snippet: Cultivating a Regional Geoscience Learning Ecosystem: Systemic Equity and Cultural Change in California’s Central Valley The geosciences remain among the least racially diverse STEM fields, with limited progress over the past four decades. This article presents a case study of the San Joaquin Valley Geoscience Learning Ecosystem, a regional initiative designed to transform institutional culture and strengthen recruitment, engagement, and persistence for first-generation, low-income, and racially/ethnically diverse students in Geology and Environmental Science undergraduate majors at two Hispanic-Serving Institutions in California: Fresno State and the State Center Community College District. The project established a student cohort program, a faculty professional learning community, and community-based research experiences grounded in culturally-relevant pedagogy, place-based learning, and project-based learning. Drawing on implementation evidence and reflective analysis, we examine STEM culture change across four interrelated dimensions: structures and formal roles, languages and symbols, people, and power and decision-making. title: Variations in Equitable Sociocultural Interactions Across Learning Activities in Pre-K to Third-Grade Classrooms
text_snippet: Variations in Equitable Sociocultural Interactions Across Learning Activities in Pre-K to Third-Grade Classrooms This study used secondary data collected in public elementary schools from 2016 to 2019 to examine variations in equitable sociocultural interactions, measured by the Assessing Classroom Sociocultural Equity Scale (ACSES), among classroom formats (e.g., whole group, small group), content domains (e.g., language and literacy, math, science), and class sizes. The sample included 348 video recordings from 65 teachers. Results indicated that teachers made more connections to children’s home lives during language and literacy lessons compared to math lessons. Additionally, teachers provided children more Personalized Learning Opportunities during centers and small-group formats compared to whole-group formats. Analyses showed no variation in Inequitable Discipline or racially marginalized learners’ Participation and Engagement by content domain, classroom format, or class size. These findings point to the potential use of ACSES for measuring culturally responsive, equitable classroom management across multiple contents and classroom activity settings.

title: An Overview of Female Researchers: Demands, Job Resources, and Mental Health Among Brazilian University Faculty
text_snippet: An Overview of Female Researchers: Demands, Job Resources, and Mental Health Among Brazilian University Faculty Mental health problems among university faculty have been increasingly associated with intensified work demands, with women being particularly vulnerable due to persistent gender inequalities in academic careers. This study examined the perceptions of women faculty members at Brazilian public universities regarding work demands, organizational resources, and institutional practices aimed at promoting mental health and gender equity, using the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model as its theoretical framework. A qualitative study was conducted with eight women faculty members from public universities across different regions of Brazil, aged between 36 and 56 years (M = 46.5, SD = 7.05), most of whom were in stable relationships and reported household incomes ranging from BRL 15,000 to BRL 30,000 per month. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s Thematic Analysis. The findings revealed that occupational overload is intensified by gender inequalities, particularly those associated with motherhood penalties and the invisibility of caregiving work. title: From Digital Integration to Digital Normalization: Generational Trends in Students’ Perception of Social Media Impact (2016–2022)
text_snippet: From Digital Integration to Digital Normalization: Generational Trends in Students’ Perception of Social Media Impact (2016–2022) This study examines how students perceive the influence of social media on everyday life across a seven-year period (2016–2022), focusing on two domains: aesthetic–consumer choices and lifestyle-related orientations. The research uses a cross-sectional design with repeated annual cohorts (N = 589) from social sciences programs, applying a questionnaire adapted from an existing instrument measuring the perceived influence of social media on consumer choices and lifestyle-related orientations. Factor analysis revealed a stable two-factor structure, while trend analysis showed that both dimensions follow a gradual and moderate upward trajectory. The influence on lifestyle is consistently higher than on aesthetic–consumer decisions, which indicates that students interpret digital content primarily through everyday routines and values rather than market-driven cues. The temporary stabilization of scores during the pandemic aligns with recent findings on digital fatigue, where increased exposure does not automatically increase perceived impact. title: Automated Generation of Individualized Electrical Circuit Exercises Using Python and LTspice: Reducing Instructor Preparation Time
text_snippet: Automated Generation of Individualized Electrical Circuit Exercises Using Python and LTspice: Reducing Instructor Preparation Time This study presents a methodology for the automatic generation of individualized electrical circuit exercise booklets using Python and LTspice and examines the academic outcomes observed after its implementation and its estimated effect on instructor preparation time. The methodology begins with the design of circuit theory exercises, which are subsequently parameterized and automatically simulated through Python scripts integrated with LTspice. Based on the simulation results, the system generates individualized exercise booklets, solution templates, and simulation files for each student while simultaneously collecting quantitative data to assess academic performance. The proposed approach enables both formative training and individualized assessment without substantially increasing the instructors’ workload. Descriptive comparison with previous academic years indicates no deterioration in academic outcomes, although the cohorts compared are not concurrent and no inferential testing was performed, so no causal claim about learning can be made. title: Developing a Professional Learning Framework for Alternatively Certified Teachers: A Delphi Study of Knowledge, Skills, and Dispositions
text_snippet: Developing a Professional Learning Framework for Alternatively Certified Teachers: A Delphi Study of Knowledge, Skills, and Dispositions Teacher shortages and expanding alternative certification pathways have intensified the need for coherent support for teachers entering classrooms through nontraditional routes. This three-round Delphi study identified professional-learning priorities for newly alternatively certified teachers. Thirty-six K-12 teachers, administrators, and teacher educators in rural and semi-rural Montana completed all three rounds. Round 1 generated 120 open-ended responses, which were refined into 108 Round 2 statements; 97 statements advanced to Round 3. The study defined consensus as a mean of at least 4.00 and a standard deviation of no more than 0.75. The supplied final item lists contained 89 rated statements: 29 knowledge, 26 skills, and 34 dispositions. Item-level verification against the supplied Round 3 summary statistics showed that 53 of the 89 statements met both criteria: 7 knowledge, 19 skills, and 27 dispositions. All 89 items are reported for transparency, together with means, standard deviations, criterion status, and provisional domain assignments. title: Arts Engagement and Character Virtues: Complementary Associations with Primary School Students’ Self-Perceived Competencies
text_snippet: Arts Engagement and Character Virtues: Complementary Associations with Primary School Students’ Self-Perceived Competencies Drawing on the Positive Development and Assessment Competencies (PDAC) model, this cross-sectional study examined whether character virtues and self-reported arts engagement make complementary contributions to primary school students’ self-perceived competencies. Data were collected from 993 fifth- and sixth-grade students; 695 provided valid responses to both arts items. Continuous competency scores were analysed using hierarchical linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors, demographic adjustment, and Benjamini–Hochberg correction. title: Exploring How Lecturers’ Behaviours Relate to Students’ Motivation to Participate in Self-Directed Learning in African Higher Education
text_snippet: Exploring How Lecturers’ Behaviours Relate to Students’ Motivation to Participate in Self-Directed Learning in African Higher Education Lecturer feedback, dialogical pedagogies, and supportive relationships are recognised as important for motivating participation in self-directed learning (SDL), yet the transferability of predominantly non-African evidence remains uncertain amid diverse African sociocultural, institutional, and resource conditions. This systematic review examined lecturer behaviours associated with African higher education students’ motivation to participate in SDL and challenges constraining lecturer practice. Searches of Web of Science, Google Scholar, Sabinet African Journals, ERIC, and African Journals Online for peer-reviewed evidence published during 2015–2026, supplemented by citation and companion-report tracing, yielded 460 records and 269 full texts; 85 publications were included: 72 empirical reports representing 63 study families, 5 reviews, and 8 conceptual publications. Thematic synthesis identified five behaviours: supporting student agency and ownership; providing psychologically safe support; using engaging instruction associated with intrinsic motivation; modelling self-direction and lifelong learning; and contextualising teaching and learning. title: How Should School-Based Educational Digital Games Be Evaluated? A Proposed Framework for Examining Experiences Beyond Isolated Metrics
text_snippet: How Should School-Based Educational Digital Games Be Evaluated? A Proposed Framework for Examining Experiences Beyond Isolated Metrics Educational digital games are increasingly incorporated into formal learning contexts. However, their evaluation often relies on isolated outcome measures that provide limited insight into how students experience, interpret, and assess gameplay. This conceptual article proposes a practice-informed critical-participatory framework for the student-centred evaluation of educational digital game experiences. The framework was developed through a practice-informed conceptual synthesis. This synthesis brought together recurring methodological concerns from school-based work and relevant scholarship on game-based learning, student participation, and mixed-methods evaluation. The framework comprises five guiding criteria: pedagogical alignment, learner and contextual suitability, multidimensionality, student participation, and triangulation. It also includes a seven-stage operationalisation extending from the definition of the educational problem to the use of findings for improvement. title: Differentiated Instruction and Learning Outcomes in Vocational Pharmacy Education: A Quasi-Experimental Study
text_snippet: Differentiated Instruction and Learning Outcomes in Vocational Pharmacy Education: A Quasi-Experimental Study Differentiated instruction has been proposed as an effective approach for addressing learner diversity and enhancing learning outcomes. The present study investigated the effects of a differentiated instructional intervention, informed by principles of cognitive psychology, Cognitive Load Theory, and educational neuroscience, on cognitive performance, learning engagement, and perceived cognitive load among vocational education students. A quasi-experimental design was implemented with 57 students enrolled in the Pharmacy Assistant specialty program of the Greek Public Employment Service Vocational Education Schools (EPAS DYPA). Two first-year and two second-year classes participated in both traditional and differentiated instructional sessions. Cognitive performance, learning engagement, and cognitive load were assessed through quizzes, application exercises, questionnaires, and rating scales. The findings indicated no statistically significant differences between instructional approaches among first-year students. title: Professional Development in Education: A Qualitative Study of Public School Teachers’ Perceptions of Meaningful Growth and Mandated Practice
text_snippet: Professional Development in Education: A Qualitative Study of Public School Teachers’ Perceptions of Meaningful Growth and Mandated Practice The present study investigates the professional development (PD) experience of ten public school teachers in British Columbia. The teachers are regular participants in school and district-based professional development (PD) programs. The research seeks to investigate whether PD is experienced as a genuine investment in professional growth or as time and resources that are wasted. Research suggests that traditional models often fail to produce deep, lasting change in practice. By investigating the professional and personal insights of teachers across grade levels and disciplines, the study identifies common themes in what makes PD meaningful, effective, or ineffective. These insights not only contribute to the understanding of teacher development but also offer practical implications for designing PD into the future that is relevant, engaging, and responsive to the realities of contemporary classrooms. The study contributes to ongoing discussions about how PD can more effectively support teacher learning as a socially mediated and contextually grounded process, affirming the value of aligning PD design with teachers’ professional agency and situated experience.

title: AI and Constructivist Pedagogy in TVET: A Scoping Review of Integration Mechanisms, Competencies, and Implementation Challenges
text_snippet: AI and Constructivist Pedagogy in TVET: A Scoping Review of Integration Mechanisms, Competencies, and Implementation Challenges The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) is reshaping instructional practices by enabling adaptive, learner-centered environments that support competency development. Reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and PRISMA-ScR, this scoping review examines how AI-integrated constructivist pedagogy facilitates competency development in TVET contexts. Searches across six databases and a manual website search identified 11 studies published between 2016 and 2025, spanning multiple regions, TVET levels, and domains. Findings indicate that problem-based learning and project-based learning are the dominant constructivist approaches, supported by generative AI and intelligent tutoring systems. AI-enabled constructivist environments were associated with strengthened technical competencies and enhanced transferable competencies including critical thinking, collaboration, and career readiness. Given the small, heterogeneous, and largely non-experimental evidence base, these findings indicate associations rather than causal effects. Adaptation and Revalidation of the General Attitude to Study Questionnaire (E-1) Vocational training, which is currently on the rise, is practical teaching that prepares students for the performance of a profession. VET students have specific characteristics that make research necessary. The objective of this study was to validate and apply a questionnaire on the general attitude towards study (E-1) to a sample of 502 VET students and to determine the implications of personal and sociodemographic variables in motivations towards learning. title: Understanding the Nature of Science (NOS): Insights from Pre-Service Teachers’ Engagement with Scientific Biographies
text_snippet: Understanding the Nature of Science (NOS): Insights from Pre-Service Teachers’ Engagement with Scientific Biographies The comprehension of the nature of science (NOS) is increasingly recognised as a crucial element of science education, and many countries have incorporated NOS-related elements into their national curricula. This development underscores the need to adequately prepare teachers to possess a thorough understanding of the fundamental principles of NOS. This article explores pre-service teachers’ understanding of NOS when engaging with scientific biography. Using biographies is proposed as a pedagogical strategy for embedding NOS within the curriculum. Grounded in the consensus view of NOS, this study evaluates students’ conceptualisations by analysing interviews and student presentations of the scientists’ life stories. The findings reveal variations in the students’ awareness concerning general aspects of NOS. Some pre-service teachers demonstrate a more profound understanding of science, recognising its tentativeness, social dependence, and the influence of human factors. title: Self-Perceived Ethical Knowledge in AI-Enhanced Teacher Education: Adaptation and Validation of a Scale for Chinese Preservice Preschool Teachers
text_snippet: Self-Perceived Ethical Knowledge in AI-Enhanced Teacher Education: Adaptation and Validation of a Scale for Chinese Preservice Preschool Teachers The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into early childhood education has led to ethical concerns regarding children’s privacy, fairness, and developmental appropriateness. While ethical knowledge is recognised as an important component of teachers’ professional knowledge, existing instruments such as the Technological Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (TPCEK) framework were developed for preservice teachers in general and do not fully capture the ethical issues specific to AI-supported preschool education. In this study, we adapted and validated a Self-Perceived Ethical Knowledge Scale for Chinese preservice preschool teachers based on the eight ethics-related dimensions of TPCEK. A two-phase sequential design was employed. In Phase 1, a three-round modified Delphi study was conducted, involving 20 experts who refined an initial 40-item pool into a 33-item scale. In Phase 2, we examined the scale’s psychometric properties by performing an exploratory factor analysis (EFA) on a pilot sample (n = 289)—with factor retention corroborated by principal-axis parallel analysis—and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) on a separate main-study sample (n = 583). title: Benchmarking Observable Platform Dynamics Beyond Persistence in Three Open Educational Datasets
text_snippet: Benchmarking Observable Platform Dynamics Beyond Persistence in Three Open Educational Datasets Educational theories of artificial intelligence (AI)-supported learning include mechanisms absent from reusable platform logs. We separated a conceptual framework from four source-derived proxies: cumulative achievement, engagement, resource breadth, and digital activity. The Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD) was primary; Eedi provided external evaluation and EdNet an exploratory transport stress test, with 72,277, 7149, and 513 lagged transitions. In the OULAD temporal holdout, observable-state ridge regression reduced root-mean-square error (RMSE) versus persistence by 14.51–15.59% for behavioral proxies but by 0.16% for achievement. Autoregression captured 98.24–99.78% of behavioral gains; cross-state predictors added 0.038–0.324% beyond autoregression. Three outcomes supported prediction beyond persistence; none supported incremental cross-state prediction or coefficient interpretation. Same-feature gradient boosting improved behavioral-proxy prediction by 0.84–2.84% but worsened achievement by 3.47%. title: A Study on Improving the Usability of an AI-Based Learning Tool to Support English Diary Writing for EFL Students
text_snippet: A Study on Improving the Usability of an AI-Based Learning Tool to Support English Diary Writing for EFL Students AI-based writing support systems are increasingly being explored as tools for supporting English writing in educational contexts. In English as a Foreign Language (EFL) settings, learners often need support in generating ideas, organizing content, receiving feedback, and revising written texts. However, AI-based writing tools should be carefully designed and evaluated to ensure their usability, reliability, and educational relevance before being implemented in authentic learning contexts. This study aimed to design and evaluate the educational usability of WriteOn, an AI-based writing support system for EFL writing tasks that integrates AI and natural language processing technologies, including GPT-API, NLTK, spaCy, and BERT. Although the system was initially designed to support English diary writing in EFL contexts, its feedback structure and system architecture were intended to be extensible to broader writing tasks. title: AI Writing Assistants in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Review of Impact, Literacy, and Policy
text_snippet: AI Writing Assistants in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Review of Impact, Literacy, and Policy AI writing tools like ChatGPT, QuillBot, and Grammarly have reshaped university writing workflows. Controlled studies show gains in grammatical accuracy, student engagement, and self-efficacy, but none of the intervention studies retained in this review directly measured critical thinking or other higher-order outcomes, leaving concerns about overreliance largely untested rather than resolved. Synthesising 68 references published between 2008 and 2025, including 42 empirical studies, this narrative review examines how students utilise generative AI, its influence on core learning outcomes, and necessary institutional adaptations for policy and assessment. To address these shifts, the paper synthesises empirical findings across diverse study designs and proposes a seven-dimension AI literacy framework alongside practical design principles for effectively integrating AI tools into modern writing instruction.

title: Navigating Affective Cues in Video-Based Instruction: The Role of Instructor Emotions and Idiom Valence in English Idiom Acquisition
text_snippet: Navigating Affective Cues in Video-Based Instruction: The Role of Instructor Emotions and Idiom Valence in English Idiom Acquisition EFL vocabulary learning is an emotionally rich process, particularly in video-based instruction where learners encounter multiple affective cues. This mixed-methods study examined whether instructors’ emotional expressions and idiom valence influence EFL learners’ idiom acquisition and learning experience. A 3 × 3 within-subjects experimental design was adopted, manipulating instructor emotion (positive, neutral, and negative) and idiom valence (positive, neutral, and negative). Forty-five undergraduate EFL learners from a university in China participated in the study. After viewing each video, participants completed an immediate idiom recall test, a perceived learning experience scale, the self-assessment Manikin scale, a cognitive load scale and an open-ended questionnaire. The results showed that neither instructor emotion nor idiom valence had a significant main effect on immediate idiom recall. However, a significant interaction effect was observed, although follow-up comparisons did not identify a robust advantage for any specific congruent or incongruent condition. These findings provide implications for the emotional design of instructional videos in EFL vocabulary learning
